title: Read a model card before use
summary: A model card explains a shared model's intended use, training information, checks and limits. Also read its licence and files before deciding to use it.
introduction: A model card explains a shared model's intended use, training information, checks and limits. Also read its licence and files before deciding to use it. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain read a model card before use
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A model card explains a shared model's intended use, training information, checks and limits. Also read its licence and files before deciding to use it.

blocks.code:
Check the model page for:
Task and supported languages
Licence and use conditions
Training and evaluation notes
Known limits
Files and code required to load it
blocks.title: Read a model card before use

blocks.text: These details help judge whether a model fits a task. A download count is not proof of safety, accuracy or permission for every use.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write one reason a highly downloaded model might not fit a local classroom tool.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not enable trust_remote_code just to bypass an error without reviewing the code it allows to run.
For more detail later, use this [Hugging Face further reading](https://huggingface.co/docs).
